memory_candidates.content: When a cross-repository hand-off provides a generated, gate-checked citation manifest (name -> file/line lookup) as the input for correcting stale line-number citations, verify completion by grepping for the exact retired strings (old declaration names, deleted file paths, deleted attributions) rather than by pattern-matching line-number prefixes -- corrected values can share a leading digit with stale ones (e.g. both start with '2'), making a naive '<file>:2' grep unable to distinguish fixed from broken. Name-first resolution (check numbers against names, never the reverse) is the reliable completion gate.

A producing repository can hand off documentation corrections to a consuming repository via a read-only 'corrections the consuming table owes' page plus a generated, checked manifest, keyed by declaration name rather than line number. The consuming side applies corrections by mechanical name-based lookup against the manifest -- never re-deriving line numbers by hand -- and treats the manifest as authoritative over any prior research report's numbers, since the producing tree can move between research and implementation.
